correctness.rationale: Re-ran verify_construction.py: brute U equals formula U (14,64,362) with |F|=(14,60,362) at n=6,7,8; formula gives |F|=2616,21518 at n=9,10. Independently rebuilt F and confirmed zero 2-intersection violations and Delta_2=|R| with gamma_2=4 at n=6,7,8 (n=8: |R|=358,|F|=362). General-n logic holds: C0-pairs share 2 fixed points, P_full-pairs share the n-3 coset equations (>=3 for n>=6), cross pairs by definition of R. Inclusion-exclusion coefficients reproduce brute pair/triple/quad intersections at n=8 (256/265,212,168). Margin |R|-((n-3)!+4) verified positive for n=7..30 with the 1/e asymptotic mechanism. DRAFT's '2<=i<=n-4' is an off-by-one typo for '2<=i<=n-3' per |M|=6 and the verified script; the headline's abstract (n-3)-coset description is correct.

originality.rationale: EMERGENT_FINDING audited with no preset presumption. Fused three-direction literature search returned Ellis (2011) first-level stability, Wang-Xiao (2025/26) t=1 diversity, Meagher-Razafimahatratra (2020) EKR, and Chase et al. (2022/26) uniqueness as nearest prior work. Full-text inspection shows Ellis's extremal D has 2 outside perms (diversity 2) with no fixed-diversity>=3 exact count; Wang-Xiao is 1-intersecting only; the EKR/uniqueness papers fix only the (n-2)! maximum with zero diversity content. No source states the 4-outside transverse (n-3)-coset family, its rook closed form, or values 14,60,362,2616,21518. Ellis's bound implies only the shared (1-1/e) constant, not the exact construction.

value.rationale: Explicit infinite 2-intersecting family at fixed diversity 4 with proved exact closed-form size, the concrete sharpness candidate for the admitted target's gamma_2>=3 maximum. Object and invariant were motivated before computation (deletion-union minimization); the value was not known or mechanically implied (nearest Ellis D is diversity 2 and strictly larger: |D|-|F|=1,9,51,307,2117 for n=6..10). Backed by n=6 exhaustive concentrated-class optimality (14=formula) and unbeaten structured probes at n<=9. A future worker on second-level permutation stability reasonably needs this exact datum; it is a genuine extremal-construction theorem, not a textbook restatement or parameter substitution.
